detail: FSD t1.r2.c3: "Calendar year of the order". The basis said that whether the date Dim Time is joined on is the order date is not recorded; the as-is section "How the tables relate" (reviewed) records SAMP_REVENUE_F joined to SAMP_TIME_DAY_D on BILL_DAY_DT (SAMP_REVENUE_F_FKey#3) and to SAMP_TIME_MTH_D on BILL_MTH_KEY, i.e. the bill date
FSD wants the calendar year of the order; the row was 55 on the name only, and the recorded join places revenue in the year of the bill date, not of the order

lookup "order date" / "order day" shows Fact Revenue.Order Day Dt (all words: order, day; not a measure; SAMP_REVENUE_F.ORDER_DAY_DT), the date of the order, from which the order year could be taken; the basis did not name it
FSD t1.r4.c3: "Brand of the product sold", a name. The row named Dim Products.Brand Key at 75, the key; lookup "brand" shows Dim Products.Brand as whole name: brand, and Brand Key under all words
the basis describes another column than the row: "column Brand, mapped from SAMP_PRODUCTS_D.BRAND; runner-up Dim Products.Brand Key"; the row's column is Brand Key (SAMP_PRODUCTS_D.BRAND_KEY)

FSD t2.r3.c3: "Number of units sold", actuals. The row named Fact Target.Units at 75 (SAMP_TARGETS_F.UNITS, the targets table); lookup "units" shows Fact Revenue.Units (whole name, SUM, table Fact Revenue) as the actual units

the basis describes another column than the row: "table Fact Revenue (the actuals), database columns SAMP_REVENUE_F.UNITS ...; runner-up Fact Target.Units, the planned units"; the row's column is Fact Target.Units

the basis said "the units part, the same as K2"; K2's row named Fact Target.Units, a different column (now unmatched). The row itself, Fact Revenue.Units at 70, fits the FSD t2.r5.c3 "divided by units sold" and the lookup

FSD p10: "X axis: month of the year". The basis said whether revenue joins on the order or the bill month is open; the as-is section "How the tables relate" (reviewed) records SAMP_REVENUE_F joined on BILL_DAY_DT and BILL_MTH_KEY and SAMP_TARGETS_F on BILL_MTH_KEY

lookup "month": all words: month, not a measure, table Dim Time; the basis itself leaves open whether the 9-character text holds the month alone or year and month, which is what "month of the year" asks; nothing beyond the name settles it, so the 60-89 band is not earned

FSD p11: "Rows: product". Lookup "product" shows Prod Dsc and Prod Dsc (Translated) both all words: product, not measures; the basis says Prod Dsc (Translated) "may fit as well"; two candidates about as good earn at most 59, and the row was 62

FSD p11: "Rows: product, then office", the sales office. The row named Dim Sales Rep.Office ID at 70 (EMPLOYEE.OFFICE_ID), the office identifier of a sales representative, an ID and not the office; lookup "office" shows Dim Offices.Office Dsc, the column proposed for F2
the basis describes another column than the row: "table Dim Offices, column Office Dsc, mapped from SAMP_OFFICES_D.OFFICE_DSC"; the row's column is in Dim Sales Rep and reads EMPLOYEE.OFFICE_ID

Q3 said nothing recorded tells whether revenue joins Dim Time on the order date, assumed the order date, and asked to bring back which date SAMP_REVENUE_F joins the time table on; the export records the join on BILL_DAY_DT and BILL_MTH_KEY (the bill date), so the question stated something the lookups do not show and asked for what is recorded. Why it matters, Assumed meanwhile and How to get the answer rewritten to state the recorded join and ask which date the FSD means

Q6 How to get the answer said "ask the sales planning team", naming a team in place of a step, and asked to look at which time column SAMP_TARGETS_F joins on, which the export records (BILL_MTH_KEY to SAMP_TIME_MTH_D); rewritten as steps with what to bring back
the basis said "the same as K2"; K2's row named Fact Target.Units, a different column (now unmatched). The row itself, Fact Revenue.Units at 75, fits FSD p11 "units sold" and the lookup
